column12: fieldDescription

Multiply how much each colony's raw size weighs on its system's dominant faction, before stability scales it and the station and patrol bonuses are added. A concealed base uses this on whichever size the Concealed bases section selects. 1 counts size as-is; below 1 flattens the gap between large and small colonies, above 1 widens it; 0 drops raw size entirely (a colony then holds a system only through its station or patrol bonus, if any). Default: 1.

How a concealed base (a hidden market such as a pirate base or the Galatia Academy) counts toward its system's dominant faction. Normal weighs it by its real colony size like any colony; Fixed folds it in at the Concealed base fixed weight below, regardless of size, so a large secret base never outweighs the open colonies around it. Both then take the colony size weight and stability. Default: Fixed.

The fixed size rating a concealed base folds in at while Concealed base scaling is Fixed, in place of its real size, before the colony size weight and stability apply. 1 counts a concealed base as a single size point; higher lets a secret base mark more presence. Ignored while Concealed base scaling is Normal. Default: 1.

Master switch for stability scaling. When on, each dominance factor (colony size, station bonus, patrols) is cut at low stability by its own low-stability penalty below, so a destabilised colony holds less of its system than a functioning one. Turn off to ignore stability entirely and rank colonies by their raw weighted size, station, and patrol sum. Default: true.

How much a colony's own size weight is cut when its stability is at zero, as a fraction: 1 removes it entirely at zero stability (half at 5, full at 10), 0.5 leaves it half its weight at zero stability, 0 ignores stability for colony size. Applies only while Stability weighs dominance is on. Default: 1.

Give a colony with an attached defensive station extra size points toward its system's dominant faction (see Station weight), so a stationed colony outranks an otherwise-identical unstationed one. A concealed base's station earns a fraction of it (see Concealed-base station fraction), and how much the bonus survives low stability is set by the Station low-stability penalty. Turn off to rank colonies without any station bonus. Default: true.

How many size points an attached defensive station adds to a visible colony's dominance contribution, before its low-stability penalty applies. 1 makes a station worth a single colony size point; below 1 softens the bonus, above 1 sharpens it; 0 removes it. A concealed base earns this scaled by the Concealed-base station fraction. Ignored while Station weighs dominance is off. Default: 1.

The fraction of the Station weight a station on a concealed base earns, so a fortified secret base reads above a bare concealed outpost without matching an openly held stationed colony. 0 gives concealed bases no station bonus; 1 gives them the full station weight. Ignored while Station weighs dominance is off. Default: 0.5.

How much the station bonus is cut when the colony's stability is at zero, as a fraction: 1 removes it entirely at zero stability, 0.5 leaves it half at zero stability, 0 keeps the full station bonus regardless of stability. Applies only while Stability weighs dominance is on. Default: 0.5.

Give a colony extra size points toward its system's dominant faction for the patrols its military bases field, weighted by patrol size (see the three patrol weights below). Reads the colony's configured patrol strength from the economy, so it counts steadily rather than tracking the fleets currently in flight. Off by default. Default: false.

How many size points each small (light) patrol a colony fields adds toward its system's dominant faction, before the patrol low-stability penalty applies. Ignored while Patrols weigh dominance is off. Default: 0.25.

How many size points each medium patrol a colony fields adds toward its system's dominant faction, before the patrol low-stability penalty applies. Ignored while Patrols weigh dominance is off. Default: 0.5.

How many size points each large (heavy) patrol a colony fields adds toward its system's dominant faction, before the patrol low-stability penalty applies. Ignored while Patrols weigh dominance is off. Default: 1.

How much a colony's patrol bonus is cut when its stability is at zero, as a fraction: 1 removes it entirely at zero stability, 0.5 leaves it half at zero stability, 0 keeps the full patrol bonus regardless of stability. Applies only while Stability weighs dominance is on. Default: 0.5.

How far each system's coloured territory extends into empty space, in world units, before its frontier edge closes it off. Higher lets each system claim more open space - distant systems' territories grow until they meet and merge; lower pulls every territory in tight around its own systems. Default: 4000.

Draw each contiguous faction cluster's name across its territory, HOI4-style, in the faction's colour. The name sits along the cluster's fitted label line - inside the border, clear of system icons, leaning along the cluster's long axis - above the fills and borders but below the vanilla star and constellation names. Default: true.

column9: insignia42LTaa, insignia25LTaa, insignia21LTaa, orbitron24aa, orbitron20aa, orbitron20aabold
column12: The antialiased LazyFont face the faction names render in, from the game's graphics/fonts folder. A name is stretched to span its cluster, far past the face's glyph-atlas resolution, so only high-resolution antialiased faces are offered - a low-resolution face turns blocky when magnified that far, while a large-atlas face stays clean. insignia42LTaa, the sharpest, is the default. Default: insignia42LTaa.

Whether each faction cluster's label spells out the owner's full name or its short name. Full draws the long-form faction name; Short draws the abbreviated name, which fits a tighter cluster at a larger font. Default: Full names.
The smallest height (world units) a line of a faction name may render at - the readability floor. A cluster too small to hold even one line this tall anywhere shows no name. Default: 200.
The largest height (world units) a line of a faction name may render at, so a roomy cluster does not draw an oversized label. The upper bound of the font-size fit. Default: 1200.

The most lines a faction name may wrap into, on word boundaries. A multi-line block is chosen only when it renders a strictly larger font than the single long line would - wrapping shortens the widest line and spends the cluster's spare girth. 1 forces single-line names. Default: 3.
The line-height multiple between a multi-line name's stacked lines, so a two- or three-line block is that much taller than the raw line heights. 1 sets the lines flush. Default: 1.15.

List every market condition in the KMU condition picker, including non-planetary ones the game does not normally offer for hand placement (such as decivilisation). Turn off to restrict the picker to the planetary conditions vanilla treats as hand-placeable. Default: true.

Dev: sides of the polygon that rounds each system cell's outer frontier - its reach into empty space. Higher is smoother but adds a vertex per segment to every frontier cell, which can cost map FPS; lower trades a faceted frontier for fewer vertices. Default: 48.

Dev: how far apart two outline points may be and still merge into one corner when chaining the border, in world units. Raise if faction borders go missing; too high merges distinct corners. Always applied - this is the raw ring tracing, upstream of the spike and rounding passes below. Default: 100.

Dev: a corner whose inset point would jut past this multiple of the border inset is bevelled flat instead of pointed. Lower bevels sharp corners sooner (no inward spikes/loops); higher keeps crisper points. Always applied - part of the inset that traces the ring, not a gated smoothing pass. Default: 4.

Dev: master switch for the spike-sanding pass in this section, which runs before corner rounding and splices out needle and cusp protrusions the rounding cannot fix. On uses the height and angle below; off skips the pass and leaves those two knobs unread, keeping their values for when you switch it back on. Default: false.

Dev: a sharp corner rising less than this (world units) above its neighbours is a needle or cusp too thin for rounding to fix, so it is sanded off before rounding; a sharp corner that juts farther is kept as real shape. Ignored while Sand border spikes is off. Default: 150.

Dev: only corners sharper than this interior angle (degrees) are candidates for spike sanding; gentler corners and smooth arc facets are kept. Pairs with spike height - a corner must be both sharp and shallow to be sanded. Ignored while Sand border spikes is off. Default: 60.

Dev: master switch for the corner-rounding pass in this section. On replaces each sharp border corner with an arc using the radius, segments, and chamfer below; off leaves the resolved envelope sharp-cornered and leaves those three knobs unread, keeping their values for when you switch it back on. Also gates the factionless (decivilised and uninhabited) cell outlines, so the whole map's corners round or not together. Default: true.

Dev: corner-rounding radius of the national border, in world units. Higher rounds the cluster outline more; the cut self-limits on short edges. Ignored while Round border corners is off. Default: 300.
Dev: arc segments per rounded corner of the national border. Higher is smoother but adds vertices. Ignored while Round border corners is off. Default: 3.
Dev: corners sharper than this interior angle (degrees) are cut flat (chamfered) instead of given a full arc. Ignored while Round border corners is off. Default: 35.

Dev: how many directions the label-anchor search fans over the half-circle (0-180 degrees; a label line is undirected). More directions let the accepted line align more closely with the cluster's open space, at a higher search cost. Pure horizontal, the cluster's own principal axis, and the preferred slant are always searched on top of the fan. Default: 9.

Dev: how many parallel lines the search sweeps across the cluster per direction, spaced evenly over the cluster's extent perpendicular to that direction. This is what lets the accepted line slide off the centroid into a roomier part of the cluster - an icon on the centre line relocates the label instead of shrinking it. 1 degenerates to a single centred line per direction. Default: 15.

Dev: how much length a shallower (more horizontal) candidate line may give up and still win the search. Each candidate's clear length is scaled by 1 - strength * sin(angle)^exponent, where angle is the line's slope from horizontal. 0 picks the pure longest line regardless of slope; 1 scores a vertical line zero. Default: 0.2.

Dev: how sharply the vertical penalty concentrates toward the perpendicular - the exponent on the line's deviation from the cluster's preferred lean in the score. A higher exponent leaves near-lean lines almost unpenalised and bites only as a line swings far off it. Default: 2.

Dev: how far a label may lean off level to follow its cluster's long axis, in degrees. The anchor search prefers this cluster-specific slant over screen-horizontal, capped here so a tall cluster never stands its name vertical and scaled down toward 0 as a cluster gets rounder (a near-round or tightly clumped cluster has no trustworthy long axis, so it stays level). 0 forces dead-horizontal labels; 90 lets a label follow its axis all the way to vertical. Default: 22.

Dev: how far short of the national border each end of a label anchor stops, in multiples of the border inset channel - the gap a faction name needs so it does not touch the border. A clear line shorter than twice this collapses to the dot. Default: 4.

Dev: the keep-out radius around each system icon that a label anchor must not cross, in world units - an approximation of the icon's on-map footprint, since icons draw at a fixed pixel size. An icon on a cluster's axis shortens the anchor to the clear side rather than letting a name run across the star. Default: 750.

Dev: the fill opacity of the debug band quad - the box the fitted label occupies, drawn over the anchor line. Kept low so the national border reads through the band and an overflow is visible; the whole point of the band is to see it kiss or clear the border. Default: 0.35.

Dev: the opacity of the debug band box's strokes - its outline, the line-count divider rules, the centreline, and the anchor dot. Kept separate from the fill so the outline can read stronger than the faint band wash it sits on. Default: 0.9.

Dev: draw every faction's colonies on the political map, including ones the player has not discovered yet - bypasses the known-to-player gate so an undiscovered colony still folds into its system's dominance, inhabitation, and cell geometry. Off by default; a reveal aid for inspecting the whole sector's politics. Default: false.

Dev: seed political-map geometry for every star system in the sector, not just the reachable, visible, or inhabited ones - forces a cell onto systems the map would otherwise omit. A forced system draws as uninhabited (no faction colour) unless it holds a colony. Off by default; a reveal aid for inspecting the full cell partition. Default: false.

Dev: draw a dot at each system cluster's centre and, in green, the fitted label line - the cluster's long axis refit to stay inside the national border, clear of system icons, and short of the border by the anchor end inset, leaning horizontal per the anchor bias. The anchor a faction name hangs on; a diagnostic for the label placement behind the faction names. Master switch for the anchor overlay - the two axis toggles below only add lines while this is on. Default: false.

Dev: when a cluster's fitted label line collapses to the dot, also draw in red the best candidate line the fit found before the border, icon, or end-margin trim discarded it - so a near miss can be told from a hopeless cluster while tuning the anchor knobs. Layered under the yellow and green lines. Only meaningful while Show cluster label anchors is on. Default: false.

Dev: also draw in yellow the label line each cluster's fit would accept with no horizontal bias applied, so the anchor bias knob's effect is visible by contrast. Skipped when the unbiased direction matches the accepted line (bias at 1, or an axis already horizontal) - the green line already is the unbiased one. Layered under the green line. Only meaningful while Show cluster label anchors is on. Default: false.

Dev: replace the normal political-map render with a border-tracing diagnostic that layers the smoothing pipeline's stages so you can see what each pass did. From bottom to top: the base traced border in red, the despiked border in yellow, and the rounded border in green. Respects the two smoothing gates - a stage draws only when its pass ran, so with sanding off there is no yellow and with rounding off no green. Off by default. Default: false.

column9: OFF, ERROR, WARN, INFO, DEBUG, ALL
column12: Verbosity of KMU's own output in starsector.log. WARN is the normal level; INFO adds routine lines and DEBUG adds per-frame overlay diagnostics. Default: WARN.
